indexPrompt.pg-a-baseline-from-the-same-batch: A policy trains on one-step episodes using the mean reward of its N sampled episodes as the baseline, and Part 1 finds the constant factor this shrinks the expected update by at N = 4. Part 2 shows a leave-one-out baseline is unbiased and rescales the estimator by N/(N-1), and Part 3 finds the smallest batch that keeps 95% of the true gradient.
indexPrompt.pg-advantages-on-the-way-to-the-dock: An actor-critic robot makes three moves into its charging dock, earning a reward at each, and a critic network values every state it lands in. Compute the one-step advantage weight for two of the moves, then weigh the first move by the Monte Carlo advantage instead and compare what each weight relies on.
indexPrompt.pg-baseline-read-one-step-late: A warehouse robot at a junction takes a shortcut whose return is 5 or a long way whose return is 1, and a slipped baseline subtracts the average return of the state the robot moves to instead of the state it acts from. Which route does the policy at the junction come to prefer as training goes on?
indexPrompt.pg-credit-across-one-episode: An agent alternates between positions A and B and picks left or right at each, with the probability of right at A equal to 0.6 and of left at B equal to 0.5. For one three-step episode with rewards +5, 0 and -2 and no discounting, compute the single-episode REINFORCE gradient component for the right-action logit at A under reward-to-go weights and under the full episode return, and say which actions each estimate pushes up and why both have the same expected value.
indexPrompt.pg-gaussian-policy-aims-at-a-target: A controller picks a continuous action from a Gaussian policy with mean mu and a fixed spread, and the reward is minus the squared distance from the action to 3. Find the expected single-sample policy-gradient estimate, its variance, and the variance after subtracting the expected reward as a baseline. Then say what happens to both variances as the spread shrinks toward zero and why one of them blows up.
indexPrompt.pg-samples-that-still-pass-a-gradient: PPO is on its third pass over a batch with epsilon 0.2, and five samples have their ratios and advantages in a table; each sample adds the minimum of the ratio times the advantage and the ratio clipped to [0.8, 1.2] times the advantage to the objective. Which of the five terms still have a nonzero gradient with respect to theta, given that each ratio itself changes with theta?
indexPrompt.pg-update-from-one-delivery: A delivery app sends each order along one of three routes with feature vectors (1, 0), (0, 2) and (2, 1), and a softmax policy over route scores picks them with probabilities 0.5, 0.3 and 0.2. One order takes route B and earns a return of 5; what is 5 times the gradient of the log probability of route B?
